scenes.headline: How a 3090 decodes several tokens per weight read
scenes.sub: Two engines for Qwen, one dense and one mixture of experts.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Wattson! Two engines run Qwen on one 3090. Each reads every weight once a cycle, and keeps several tokens from that read.

scenes.text: Decode speed is bytes per cycle over the memory bus, times the tokens each cycle commits. Engines differ in what they let count as a commit.
scenes.mark: what they let count as a commit
scenes.say: Speed is the bytes a cycle reads, over the bus, times the tokens it keeps. The engines differ in what counts as kept.

steps.say: A drafter guesses the next few tokens. They become rows of one batch.
The big model streams its four bit weights once, for every row together.
A rule decides which guesses to keep. That rule is where the engines part ways.

left.title: The dense engine
items: Nibbles become bf16 with one lop3
left.say: The dense engine turns each nibble into a sixteen bit float with one bit trick.

right.title: The llama.cpp fork
items: Weights and activations go to int8
A trellis code decoded with dp4a
right.say: The llama.cpp fork goes to eight bit integers, decodes a trellis code, and by default keeps some drafts exact sampling rejects.

scenes.title: The ceiling
scenes.text: tok/s <= L x B x e / D

parts.note: 13.554 GB per verify pass, from the headers
parts.say: D is the bytes one pass reads, counted from the checkpoint headers.
B is the bus, nine hundred thirty six gigabytes a second.
L is the tokens each cycle keeps. Only a drafter can grow it.

scenes.title: The mb-MTP rule
scenes.say: The lossy rule, in four steps.

items.say: Exact sampling rejects it just often enough to keep the target's distribution.
On a rejection, it draws a replacement.

items.text: Keep d if the target agrees
items.say: This rule keeps the draft anyway if the target likes it as much. Each rescue moves the output.

scenes.label: extra acceptance per token, and the same distance from the target
scenes.say: On a real pair, it kept five point eight to seven point five percent more tokens, and moved the output as much.

scenes.text: Both engines live on the same bus. Compare their speeds only with the same acceptance rule switched on.

recap: Speed is bytes per cycle times tokens kept
Lossy acceptance buys speed with drift
scenes.say: Bytes times tokens kept. Two routes into tensor cores. A lossy rule that trades drift for speed.
